Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States  Mixed  on hold / hawkish-leaning transition
🇪🇺 European Union  Bullish  steady ECB / growth upside
🇨🇳 China  Bearish  easing bias / weak domestic demand
🇯🇵 Japan  Bullish  pro-growth vote / tolerant yen
🇵🇱 Poland  Bullish  late easing / strong growth
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Guidance over beats: the market pays for AI that earns and sells AI that costs
🔍 Underowned Themes — Active on X, Underweight in Portfolios
India after the US tariff reset
US natural gas after the storm-spike collapse
Bitcoin breaks its floor: a liquidity event in a policy vacuum
Dollar bounce, parallel rates drift, and credit's software problem
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
Alphabet and Amazon: the capex tolerance test
$AMD  a soft guide breaks the second-source story  ↓
BitMine & Strategy / BMNR, MSTR  "leveraged crypto treasuries"
body: Wednesday, February 04 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: Growth is running hotter than sentiment: the January ISM manufacturing PMI printed 52.6% while consumer confidence fell to its lowest since 2014. The BLS delayed the January jobs report because of the partial shutdown, and traders read Kevin Warsh as a more hawkish pick for chair. Firm factories, weak households and a hawkish-leaning transition argue for a Fed on hold, not the cuts the White House wants.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.57% and the 10Y at 4.28%, a 10Y−2Y spread of 71 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03). Both rose 11 bps over 20 observations, so the spread change was 0 bps: a bear-steepening label on what is in substance a parallel sell-off, with the curve moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03). Equities slipped from near-record levels: the S&P 500 fell 0.8% to 6,917.81 and the VIX jumped 10.2% to 18.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

New / Most Important: The market's problem is AI disruption, not the economy: Wall Street ended sharply down on AI fears as new AI tools wiped $300 billion off software and data stocks, and the damage spread to Blackstone, alternative managers and BDCs as software woes infected private credit. On trade, the deal cutting US tariffs on India to 18% removes one overhang.

Playbook ✓: Keep equity beta near benchmark but rotate into energy and AI-capex industrials (XLE, XLI), funded from seat-based software, and hold 2Y–5Y Treasuries rather than the long end while the 30Y sits at 4.90% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03). Add duration only if the delayed payrolls print shows a clear labour downturn or the 10Y falls back through its 20-observation-ago 4.17%; turn defensive if the VIX holds above 18.00 while HYG makes new lows.

Macro Stance: The euro area heads into the ECB meeting from strength: Q4 GDP unexpectedly grew 0.3% and banks drove European stocks to a record high. A central bank that can sit on hold while growth surprises upward is the best setup for European cyclicals and lenders.

Credit & Inflation: The caution flag is credit: the ECB's survey shows euro-zone banks tightening access to business credit, and the German 30-year yield climbed to its highest since 2011 — a term-premium warning for long-duration assets. The STOXX 600 closed at 617.93, up 2.1% over 20 sessions, and EUR/USD slipped 0.4% to 1.1799 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

New / Most Important: AI disruption crossed the Atlantic: RELX and Wolters Kluwer plunged on AI competition fears. The DAX is down 0.5% over 20 sessions while the FTSE 100 is up 1.9% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): bank- and resource-heavy indices are beating those with software and industrial-tech weight.

Playbook ✓: Overweight euro-area banks and industrial cyclicals; underweight information-services and data publishers until AI pricing pressure is visible in guidance. Keep long-end Bund exposure light while the 30-year sits at post-2011 highs. Change the call if the next PMIs or lending survey show tighter credit biting into activity.

Macro Stance: China is a two-speed economy: exporters and high-tech manufacturers carry growth while household and property demand keep sliding. The first fiscal revenue drop since 2020, driven by the property slump and weak consumption, shows how narrow the base has become. We stay bearish on the domestic-demand complex and selective on exporters and policy beneficiaries.

PMIs & Activity: The January official manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.3, while the private survey showed factory activity growing at the fastest pace since October and beating the official reading. The gap is the story: the private gauge leans to export-oriented and private firms, the official one to large domestic and state-linked producers. Until the official index recovers, the domestic economy is not turning.

Credit Impulse: The latest credit read (December) was weak: 2025 new bank loans were the lowest in seven years, with Reuters noting policy support is needed. Easing has lowered funding costs but not created borrowers, so we read the credit impulse as still negative. A January print with rising household loans would be the first confirmation of a turn; the feed carries none yet.

Property: Property remains the drag: sales declines accelerated in a 'bleak start' to 2026 for the sector. Beijing's measures so far support prices and developer funding rather than demand, which is why developer equities rally on policy headlines and then fade. Until new-home sales stabilise, property-linked banks and building materials are funding sources, not holdings.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Fiscal firepower is being rationed — the revenue drop limits room for a large consumption push — while trade frictions keep shifting: Washington's $12 billion minerals stockpile is designed to counter China. That stockpile, set against Xi's call for the renminbi to attain reserve-currency status, shows both sides building strategic buffers rather than de-escalating, which favours China's upstream and state champions over consumer exposure.

Markets & Flows: The Shanghai Composite rose 1.3% to 4,067.74 but is down 0.4% over 20 sessions, and the Hang Seng gained 0.2% to 26,834.77 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). KWEB fell 1.9% to 34.42 and is down 5.6% over 20 sessions as Chinese tech stocks slid to the brink of a bear market on tax concerns. ASHR closed at 33.24, down 1.3% over 20 sessions, FXI is down 3.0%, and USD/CNY eased to 6.9463, a 0.6% yuan gain over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

New / Most Important: The currency is the new driver: Xi has called for the renminbi to attain global reserve-currency status, and the yuan's 0.6% gain against the dollar over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) is consistent with managed appreciation. A firmer yuan supports A-share inflows and importers but squeezes exporters' margins — the very sector carrying growth. Separately, the tax scare that hit Chinese tech shows platform regulation risk has not gone away.

Playbook ✓: Prefer onshore A-shares (ASHR) and yuan exposure over Hong Kong-listed internet names (KWEB) until the tax concern is resolved; avoid developers and property-linked lenders. Add to China cyclicals only on a January credit print with rising household loans or an official PMI back above 50. ⚠ Divergence: the private manufacturing PMI's fastest growth since October says activity is firmer than the official 49.3 suggests.

Macro Stance: Japan is Asia's cleanest pro-growth trade: polls show PM Takaichi's party poised for a landslide, which would give the government room for fiscal support and a tolerant stance on the yen. USD/JPY at 155.44 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) shows currency markets already lean that way.

Activity & Currency: Japanese stocks jumped more than 3% to a record high: the Nikkei 225 rose 3.9% to 54,720.66 and is up 5.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). USD/JPY rose 0.7% over five sessions but is down 0.8% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), so the yen has stabilised rather than collapsed — a better backdrop for domestic earners than for exporters.

Playbook ✓: Own Japanese equities with the currency hedged, favouring banks and domestic cyclicals over exporters already priced for a weak yen. Keep a small long-yen option as the hedge against an earlier BOJ hike or intervention. Cut exposure if the expected landslide fails to materialise or JGB yields spike.

Macro Stance: Australia reversed course with a rate hike and markets are betting on more: the RBA raised the cash rate 25bps to 3.85%. A central bank re-tightening straight after an easing cycle is telling markets it no longer treats inflation as transitory, and domestic demand will carry the cost.

Demand & Financing: Mortgage holders absorb a hike first, while bank margins widen as loans reprice. AUD/USD closed at 0.6956, up 3.6% over 20 sessions, and the ASX 200 rose 0.9% to 8,857.10 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): the currency, not equities, is the cleaner expression of a hawkish RBA.

Playbook ✓: Underweight rate-sensitive domestic cyclicals and REITs; prefer the major banks, which gain from loan repricing, and keep a long-AUD bias while markets price further hikes. Reverse if monthly CPI rolls over or unemployment jumps, which would end the hiking talk.

Monetary & Activity: Poland pairs strong growth with low inflation: GDP grew 3.6% in 2025, and December inflation came in below the midpoint of the NBP target (Polish: 'Inflacja w grudniu 2025 stanęła poniżej środka celu NBP'). The MPC decision is pending, and Credit Agricole economists expect an NBP rate cut ('przewidują obniżkę stóp NBP'). With inflation inside the band a cut is affordable; a hold would keep real rates high and the zloty firm.

FX & Markets: EUR/PLN closed at 4.2200, up just 0.2% over 20 sessions, and USD/PLN at 3.5768 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). The WIG20TR ETF rose 2.1% to 68.38 and EPOL 1.8% to 38.35, led by KGHM up 8.9% to 340.00, Pekao up 4.8% and PKO BP up 3.2% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Companies: KGHM is the market's metals lever: it lost 15% at the open during the metals rout and is still up 14.7% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). CD Projekt fell 3.5% to 250.70 and is down 5.7% over five sessions as Google's playable-world AI model weighs on video-game stocks, while Allegro is down 7.1% and Dino 7.5% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): gaming and consumer names lag the bank- and metals-led rally.

Security & New Development: Defence is becoming a domestic capital-markets theme: Poland awarded the Kongsberg-PGZ consortium a $1.65B counter-drone system contract, a multi-year order stream for state-owned PGZ and its domestic suppliers that keeps security spending, not just consumption, as a growth driver.

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight Poland via EPOL and the WIG20TR ETF with banks (PKO BP, Pekao) and PZU as the core: a hold protects margins, and a cut would read as growth-supportive. Trade KGHM tactically around copper, keep Allegro and Dino underweight, and fade EUR/PLN spikes above 4.2200 if the MPC holds. ⚠ Divergence: index strength leans on KGHM, whose 8.9% jump came days after a 15% opening loss — a narrower, more commodity-driven rally than the growth story implies.

Narrative: Consensus still treats AI as a tailwind for all of tech; the market now prices it as a disruptor of software economics, with new AI tools wiping $300 billion off software and data stocks. XLK fell 2.2% in the prior session and is down 1.8% over 20 sessions, with Microsoft down 14.4% over five sessions and Oracle down 19.7% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: Microsoft lost $357 billion in market value as the stock plunged the most since 2020 after its results, the clearest case of AI spending being punished. Palantir beat estimates and the stock rallied, rising 6.9% to 157.88 in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

EPS Upside Watch: Storage and memory hardware carry the cleanest estimate momentum: TrendForce sees chip prices up 90-95% quarter on quarter in Q1, straight into memory margins and against device makers' costs. Apple is up 4.3% over five sessions to 269.48 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), with component costs the swing factor for its margin guide.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Palantir rallied on the same day software was dumped: the market is separating platforms that sell AI outcomes from seat-based applications that AI can replace. Short per-seat SaaS baskets rather than XLK outright.

Narrative: Communication services is a two-megacap sector with a split tape: Meta jumped 10% on a stronger revenue forecast, while Netflix is down 12.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). XLC fell 1.6% in the prior session and is flat over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: Meta's stronger revenue forecast shows the market will pay for AI spend once it shows up in ad revenue. Legacy media is getting the opposite treatment: Disney is down 5.8% over five sessions to 104.22 and 8.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): investors are not paying for content owners without a visible AI revenue line.

EPS Upside Watch: Alphabet is set up to surprise, with results Wednesday and traders ramping long bets toward a $350 share price. GOOGL closed at 339.71, up 7.3% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Alphabet is now a disruptor inside its own sector: its prompt-to-playable-world AI model knocked video-game stocks. Owning the platform while avoiding the content and services layers it can automate is the trade the market is rewarding.

Narrative: Financials are splitting between balance-sheet banks and asset-light models exposed to AI: Blackstone, alternative managers and BDCs dived as software woes infected private credit, while money-centre banks held up. XLF fell 0.9% and is down 4.6% over 20 sessions, but JPMorgan rose 2.2% and Bank of America 0.8% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: PayPal sank on a CEO exit and a disappointing 2026 profit forecast, and Goldman Sachs slipped 0.8% to 938.99 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): payments and capital-markets franchises are being de-rated while deposit-funded lenders hold up.

EPS Upside Watch: Mortgage originators have operating leverage to mortgage rates holding near three-year lows, and banks earn more on a 71 bps 10Y−2Y spread that is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03). Net interest income, not trading, is where 2026 estimates can rise.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Banks drove European stocks to a record high while US alternative managers were sold: the market pays for regulated balance sheets and sells the private-credit model that was supposed to replace them. Long JPM and BAC against an alternative-manager basket captures the split.

Narrative: Energy is the market's hedge of choice: XLE rose 3.2% in the prior session and 10.2% over 20 sessions, with Exxon up 14.7% and Brent up 9.0% to $67.33 over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Oil climbed 2% after the US shot down an Iranian drone, so geopolitics, not demand, is setting the marginal price.

Reported: Exxon and Chevron are producing record amounts of oil, but lower prices led to lower earnings; Chevron is still up 8.7% over 20 sessions to 178.04 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), so the market is paying for volume resilience.

EPS Upside Watch: Gulf Coast refiners: the US is soon to issue a general licence for oil production in Venezuela, adding the heavy barrels complex US refiners are built to run — a crack-spread tailwind more dependable than the crude price itself.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The price risk is two-sided: oil settled down over 4% on a single day of US-Iran de-escalation. With XLE up 10.2% over 20 sessions on what is largely a risk premium (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), a diplomatic breakthrough would hit energy equities first.

Narrative: Industrials are the cleanest beneficiary of AI capex without the software-disruption risk: XLI is up 5.7% over 20 sessions and Caterpillar 14.1%, including 10.0% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). The January ISM at 52.6% says the broad factory cycle is turning up as well.

Reported: Caterpillar rose on revenue and earnings beats driven by demand for power-generation equipment, and GE Vernova's Q4 gas-turbine orders surged 74%. GE closed at 309.93, up 4.2% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

EPS Upside Watch: Power equipment remains supply-constrained: turbine orders up 74% are backlog that converts into revenue over several years, so revisions for gensets, turbines and switchgear should keep rising. Boeing, down 4.7% over five sessions to 233.15 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), is the laggard to watch as aerospace rejoins the cycle.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The policy backlash is starting: Washington state is debating making data centres pay full power costs. If hyperscalers carry more of the grid bill, data-centre timelines stretch — a risk for an AI-power trade that consensus treats as one-way.

Narrative: Discretionary is where the K-shaped economy bites: consumer confidence fell to its lowest since 2014. XLY fell 0.8% in the prior session and is up only 0.6% over 20 sessions, with Tesla down 6.6% and Nike 5.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: Chipotle forecast weak annual sales and margin pressure as consumers cut discretionary spending, while Home Depot, up 10.8% over 20 sessions to 381.10 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), is bid on housing hopes rather than current demand.

EPS Upside Watch: Amazon reports Thursday, with options pricing a large post-earnings move; AWS growth against capex is the swing factor. AMZN is down 2.5% over five sessions to 238.62 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), so expectations into the print are lower than for Alphabet.

⚡ Breaking Convention: PepsiCo plans to cut snack prices even as its drink sales improve: consumer pushback is strong enough to force price cuts on a staples giant, so discretionary pricing power is weaker still. Value formats and off-price retail win; brands that rely on price increases lose.

Narrative: Staples have become the momentum defensive: XLP rose 1.6% in the prior session and is up 11.0% over 20 sessions, with Walmart up 9.2% over five sessions and Costco 11.7% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Walmart became the first retailer to reach a $1 trillion market value.

Reported: PepsiCo's drink sales are improving, but it is planning to cut snack prices — volume recovery bought with margin. The market's preference is clear: scale retailers that turn price cuts into traffic (Walmart, Costco) over brand owners that must fund them.

EPS Upside Watch: Walmart's scale lets it convert price investment into share gains, the main source of estimate upgrades in a stretched consumer economy. Costco at 977.92 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) offers the same model with membership-fee leverage.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Staples are now crowded: an 11.0% 20-session gain for XLP (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) is a momentum move, not a valuation-led defensive rotation, and price cuts in packaged snacks cap the earnings upside. Own the retailers, not the packaged-food basket.

Narrative: Healthcare is cheapening on pricing risk: XLV fell 1.0% in the prior session and is down 0.6% over 20 sessions, with UnitedHealth down 16.9% over 20 sessions and Lilly down 3.9% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Novo Nordisk's forecast of a steep 2026 sales drop set the tone for the obesity complex.

Reported: Merck topped quarterly estimates but posted modest 2026 guidance as generic competition looms — the sector pattern of beats with cautious guides. In a market that pays for guidance, big pharma stays range-bound until pipelines replace patent-expiry revenue.

EPS Upside Watch: Lilly carries the operational upside: its CEO says Medicare coverage of obesity drugs could 'change the game' for its pill launch. Volume from broader coverage can offset price cuts in a way Novo's guide does not reflect.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Novo's warning dragged Lilly lower in sympathy, but a lower price per patient with expanding coverage is a share-shift story, not a demand collapse. The contrarian trade is long Lilly against Novo, not short the obesity theme.

Narrative: Materials are being re-rated as strategic assets: XLB is up 8.8% over 20 sessions and Freeport-McMoRan 18.9%, with copper up 4.5% to $6.06/lb in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Washington's $12 billion minerals stockpile and China's plan to expand strategic copper inventories put state buyers under the metals.

Reported: Gold posted its biggest daily gain since 2008, closing at $4,935, up 6.1%, while Freeport rose 6.4% and Newmont 3.8% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Miners are trading as leveraged metal proxies into their own reports.

EPS Upside Watch: Copper producers have the clearest estimate upside: copper is up 2.3% over 20 sessions even after the metals rout (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), and it is the AI data-centre and grid-capex metal. Producers that can supply the US stockpile gain a price floor that spot exposure lacks.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Precious metals have become a volatility asset: silver jumped 8.2% in the prior session but is down 21.3% over five sessions, and GLD fell 4.6% over five sessions before its 6.4% rebound (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Treat gold and silver miners as beta, not as portfolio hedges.

Narrative: Real estate sits between falling mortgage rates and a sticky long end: mortgage rates are holding near three-year lows, but the 10Y is up 11 bps over 20 observations to 4.28%, and XLRE slipped 0.4% in the prior session, up just 0.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03; US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: No bellwether REIT result in the feed window moved the group; price action is set by rates. With the 10Y up 11 bps and the 30Y up 5 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03), long-lease REITs get no help from duration.

EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre and powered-land landlords: the $3 trillion AI data-centre build-out has become all-consuming for debt markets, which favours REITs with cheap capital, secured power and pre-leasing over developers that need fresh debt.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Mortgage rates near three-year lows have not produced a housing-led REIT rally because affordability, not rates alone, is binding; residential landlords and builders need volume, and the feed shows no sign of it yet. Prefer data-centre and healthcare landlords over residential.

Narrative: Barron's calls American Electric Power the safer AI trade, and the tape agreed in a risk-off session: XLU rose 1.5% and NextEra 2.9%, with NextEra up 9.2% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Merchant generators are the opposite story — Constellation is down 24.4% and Vistra 6.1% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: NextEra is betting on gas as its data-centre pipeline holds steady at about 15 GW. Contracted demand with regulated returns is what the market is paying for, while merchant exposure to power-price politics is being sold.

EPS Upside Watch: Regulated utilities with rate-base growth from data-centre interconnections, such as AEP and NextEra, have the most visible EPS growth. Merchant IPPs (CEG, VST) have more upside to power prices but carry cost-allocation risk.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The political backlash is building: Washington state's debate on making data centres pay full power costs is a template for cost allocation elsewhere. The merchant IPPs' 20-session slump says the market fears price caps more than it values scarcity.

Narrative: European autos remain a structural underweight: the SXAP tracker is down 4.4% over 20 sessions, with BMW down 5.8%, Stellantis 12.3% and Renault 12.7%, Renault falling 4.2% in the prior session alone (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). One in 10 cars sold in Europe is now made by a Chinese brand.

Reported: No major European carmaker reported in the feed window; the group traded on competition and tariffs. Volkswagen preference shares slipped 0.5% to 102.25 and are down only 0.8% over 20 sessions, holding up better than peers (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

EPS Upside Watch: German premium brands have a tariff tailwind: India will slash tariffs on high-end EU cars from 110% to 30%. Mercedes held up best, up 2.8% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), and is the cleanest way to own that upside.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Chinese brands' one-in-10 share means price competition hits Europe's volume segment first, while premium makers face it mainly in China. The better trade is long Mercedes and BMW against Renault and Stellantis rather than a blanket sector short.

Narrative: Semis are in a memory-led supercycle: TrendForce sees chip prices surging 90-95% in Q1 from the previous quarter. SOXX is up 8.7% over 20 sessions despite a 2.0% drop in the prior session, led by Micron up 34.4%, Intel 25.1% and ASML 13.7% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: AMD predicted weaker first-quarter sales and the shares plunged on Nvidia comparisons. Broadcom is down 6.7% over 20 sessions and Nvidia 4.1% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): the market is rotating from compute to memory and equipment.

EPS Upside Watch: Memory makers and equipment suppliers: price increases of that scale flow largely to gross margin, and ASML at 1,395.88 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) benefits as memory makers add capacity. TSM, up 4.2% over 20 sessions to 335.75, has lagged and offers cheaper leading-edge exposure (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Customers are pushing back on the AI leader: OpenAI is reportedly unsatisfied with some Nvidia chips and looking for alternatives. That could help custom silicon and second-source GPUs over time, but for now the spend is flowing to memory, not to Nvidia's challengers.

Rewarded: Meta jumped 10% on a stronger revenue forecast, Palantir rallied after beating estimates, and Caterpillar rose on beats driven by power-generation demand. Over 20 sessions Caterpillar is up 14.1% and Micron 34.4% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): owners of AI bottlenecks are being paid.

Punished: Microsoft plunged the most since 2020, losing $357 billion of market value; PayPal sank on a CEO exit and a weak 2026 profit forecast; AMD fell as its first-quarter forecast disappointed; and Novo's steep 2026 sales-drop forecast hit the obesity complex.

Pattern: Beats are table stakes; the reaction is set by the guide and by who carries the AI cost. Investors rewarded Meta's revenue forecast and punished Microsoft's results because Meta showed AI revenue while Microsoft showed AI spending. Companies selling into the bottleneck (memory, power equipment) are rewarded; those whose product AI can replicate are sold even on beats.

Attention into EPS: Alphabet reports Wednesday and Amazon Thursday, with Eli Lilly also on the week's slate. The hyperscaler question is capex against cloud revenue: whichever shows more cloud growth per dollar of capex will be treated like Meta, the other like Microsoft.

Playbook: Into prints, own the bottleneck (memory, power equipment, grid) and avoid paying up for capex-heavy names without revenue acceleration. Sell beats with soft guides on the first rally; buy guide-raisers on the first pullback. Change the call if Alphabet and Amazon both raise capex and are rewarded — that would mean the market is paying for AI spend again.

Attention Gap: The US cut tariffs on India to 18% while India agreed to end Russian oil purchases, removing the largest single overhang on Indian exporters. The deal turns India from a tariff casualty into a beneficiary of supply-chain diversification away from China — a re-rating that rarely completes in one session.

Exposure & Risk: Express through broad India ETFs (INDA, EPI) tilted to financials and industrials rather than IT services, which dived 6% as Anthropic's AI plug-ins shook the staffing-intensive sector. Risks: the deal's terms still need detail, and India's IT exporters face the same AI-disruption repricing as US software, which caps index-level upside.

Attention Gap: Henry Hub gas fell 52.4% over five sessions to $3.31/MMBtu and is down 6.0% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), a collapse that reads as a weather unwind rather than a demand break. The structural bid is intact: Qatar Energy's CEO says AI power needs may turn the LNG glut into a gap by 2030, and NextEra is leaning on gas for its data-centre pipeline.

Exposure & Risk: Use gas-weighted producers (EQT) or LNG exporters (Cheniere) rather than front-month futures, whose roll costs and weather sensitivity dominate returns. Risks: a mild end to winter could pin prices near current levels, and power-price politics may cap how much gas-fired generators can pass through.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was $75,633.55, down 3.9% on the day, 10.6% over five sessions and 22.0% over 20 sessions; ether closed at $2,227.56, down 33.6% over 20 sessions, and solana at $97.56, down 33.5% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). IBIT is down 19.0% over 20 sessions, Coinbase 29.5% and Strategy 19.1% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Bitcoin briefly broke below $73,000, its lowest since November 2024.

New / Most Important: The selloff is a liquidity event layered on a policy vacuum. Strategy's shares slid after bitcoin briefly dipped below the firm's key breakeven level, turning the largest corporate holder from a source of demand into a source of stress. A Fed chair pick that traders read as hawkish removes the easy-money narrative, and the dollar's 1.3% five-session bounce (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) tightened the liquidity crypto runs on.

Playbook: Bearish. Do not catch the knife until bitcoin reclaims the $79,000 rebound level; a break of the $73,000 intraday low opens room to the next round-number supports. Prefer spot exposure via IBIT over leveraged proxies (MSTR, BitMine) and hedge with puts rather than outright shorts given squeeze risk. Turn constructive on stabilising ETF flows or a regulatory breakthrough on stablecoins.

Rates & Dollar: DXY closed at 97.44, up 1.3% over five sessions after the Warsh nomination but down 0.8% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).
